title: Steer a current plan
current: Steering runs the main-session flow from the hand-started session's startup block until the user's full scope is done. It helps the user write goals and a high-level strategy plan from their input, splits it into parallel dashes, records ordering needs as dependency edges only for shared files or required results instead of hand-made waves, keeps chains flat and attaches each edge at the earliest stage that works, and vets each with a subagent for overengineering. It vets every item before staffing it, including items others filed, and puts vet fixes into the spec first. Prefer simplifying or deleting and avoid new DB fields or migrations. It files vetted dashes itself and keeps the strategy doc current with short plain-language bullets; it asks the user only key decisions, as decision requests, one at a time with a recommendation. Explicit operator choices of Blitz, epic or task remain available. Major scope proposals explain what they add, why and the simplest alternative, including DB changes; they need explicit approval through a decision request, and reviewers check for these too. Anything Yoke should have done automatically but did not is a defect: before manual recovery, root-cause it with a subagent and file feedback; never report a workaround as routine. Standing decision, commit, verification-failure and discard rules live in the always-loaded AGENTS.md managed block. As work lands, seek decisions for the next set or vet and file it when clear. After failed item delivery QA, confirm and staff correction ownership, arrange qualifying delivery, preserve the original owner, inspect notice delivery and arrange supported resume/restaff if the surface lacks automatic wake. A dependency notice reports facts; activation GO remains a steering instruction, manual by design rather than a missing automatic wake. PRINCIPAL-level launches, including restaff, require explicit operator approval because they consume far more tokens; ordinary staffing is unchanged. Every steering reply ends with Needs you: and each open operator ask on one line, or Nothing needs you.
